{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: autofix.ci  # needed to securely identify the workflow

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [ "main" ]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  autofix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
      - run: corepack enable
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
        with:
          node-version: lts/-1
          cache: "pnpm"
      - run: pnpm install
      - name: Fix lint issues
        run: pnpm run lint:fix
      - uses: autofix-ci/action@7a166d7532b277f34e16238930461bf77f9d7ed8 # 7a166d7532b277f34e16238930461bf77f9d7ed8
        with:
          commit-message: 'style: apply lint fixes'
",
  "rationale": "Add a custom job timeout (timeout-minutes: 5) to the single autofix job, per pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT. The repository has representative successful-duration history (five successful runs, roughly 19-57 seconds each), so a five-minute bound provides ample headroom and cannot cause false timeouts on valid runs. The experiment example for this pattern shows adding timeout-minutes: 5 reduced median elapsed time while preserving all successes. All existing steps and required checks are preserved; no permissions, secrets, deployment, or network changes are introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
